fields.meta_title: Anonymous Mental Health Survey Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a mental health survey for staff or program check-ins that keeps answers anonymous and shows support contacts after a low answer.
fields.h1: Build a Mental Health Survey With Anonymous Answers
fields.hero_description: Build a mental health survey that keeps names off the ratings, hides teams below a minimum, and saves answers to your database.
fields.features_heading: How the Survey Handles Sensitive Answers
fields.features_subheading: Three parts govern what is stored and shown. Two put support within reach of the person answering, and one is the code.
fields.feature_1:
No names stored with any rating

Each answer is saved with the team and the date, and nothing else about the person. The survey link needs no login, and the response table has no field that names anyone.
fields.feature_2:
Team scores wait for a minimum

A team's score stays hidden until it reaches the answer count you set, 8 for example. Answers from smaller teams still count toward the company score, with no view of their own.
fields.feature_3:
Identical statements, every round

The check-in asks the same statements in the same words each time, so this quarter's score sits beside last quarter's. A drop past your threshold emails HR the team's results.
fields.feature_4:
Help numbers on the next screen

Picking the lowest option on the coping question opens a screen with your EAP number and the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. Everyone else sees both on the final screen.
fields.feature_5:
Call requests kept apart from ratings

An optional last question offers a call from your support team. A yes saves a first name and phone number to a separate list that never links back to that person's ratings.
fields.feature_6:
Your check-in's code, on GitHub

Export the survey's full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans, including the questions, scoring rules, and support screen. Your IT team can review it before launch.

fields.usecase_heading: Where Teams Run a Mental Health Survey
fields.tab_content_1:
Support drops 4 points and the HR lead hears first

Each quarter, Kittering Software's staff rate the same wellbeing statements, and a team's score shows once 8 people answer. Support fell from 15 to 11 this quarter. Any drop of 3 points or more emails HR lead Margit Osterholt, who had it before Friday's all-hands. Legal stayed hidden, short of the minimum.
fields.tab_content_2:
A call request that never touches the ratings

Nurses on the cardiac ward at Pellham Valley Hospital scan a QR code in the break room after a block of night shifts and answer 4 questions on their phone. The last offers a call from Staff Support. Ilse tapped yes. Her first name and phone number went to the call list, and her 3 ratings were saved without them.
fields.tab_content_3:
Week 8 scores, ready for the funder

Cobbleton Peer Collective runs an 8-week peer support group, and every participant rates the same statements in week 1 and again in week 8. Of the 26 who started, 22 answered both times. Their average rose from 9 to 14, and coordinator Ruairi Banfield sent the funder that change along with the anonymous comments.
fields.tab_content_4:
The support screen after a hard answer

The morning after a bus collision at its North depot, Marrowfield Transit sends all 64 drivers a 4-question check-in. Question 2 asks how each driver is coping. A driver who picks Not coping well goes straight to a screen with the employee assistance line and the 988 Lifeline, then returns to the survey.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Mental Health Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up a mental health survey that people can answer anonymously, with help numbers for anyone who needs them.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the results will change
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the anonymity rules before launch
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the one decision the answers will feed, such as a workload review for one team or another term of the peer program. If no decision depends on the results yet, wait to run the survey until one does.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose a published wellbeing scale, copy its statements word for word, and keep them fixed for every round. Add two or three questions about work itself, such as workload or manager support, and finish with one optional comment box.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Leave out name, email, and login fields, and keep only the team and the date with each answer. Choose the smallest group whose score may show, such as 8 people. State both rules on the first screen, in one plain sentence each.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask your employee assistance provider for its phone number and hours, then call the number yourself to check it. Put it on the final screen with the 988 Lifeline, and show that screen straight after the lowest answer on the coping question.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Put it all in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Type the scale, the work questions, the anonymity rules, and the support screen into one prompt. Emergent builds the survey, a response database, and a dashboard that scores each team. Prompt again to change a question or the alert threshold.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the link to five people outside the teams being surveyed, and ask one of them to pick the lowest coping answer on purpose. Then open the database and confirm that no rating row holds a name and that the support screen appeared.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share one change within a month
fields.howto_step_7_des: Within a month of closing the round, share the overall score and the one change it led to, such as an extra hire for Support. Keep next quarter's statements identical, and the following round will show whether the change worked.

faq_plan.q: What are some mental health surveys?
faq_plan.ref: what are some mental health surveys
faq_plan.a: They come in three broad kinds. Population studies, such as the World Mental Health Surveys, interview large samples of adults country by country. Short wellbeing scales score how someone has felt recently. Organization check-ins pair one of those scales with a few questions about work or a program, and they are the kind a team runs for its own people.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a mental health survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI survey builder in plain English: the statements people rate, the rule that answers carry no names, the minimum team size for results, and the help numbers on the last screen. Emergent builds the mental health survey and its database from that description. Run one test round with a few colleagues before the real invite.

faq_plan.q: Which mental health survey questions should I ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with a published wellbeing scale and use its wording unchanged. The WHO-5, for example, is a short questionnaire consisting of 5 simple and non-invasive questions. Add two questions about causes you can act on, such as hours worked and time off, and one about whether people know where to get help. Leave diagnosis questions to clinicians.

faq_plan.q: Is there a mental health survey template I can start from?
faq_plan.a: Yes, but treat any template as a first draft. Keep the scale's statements exactly as published, swap the work questions for ones about your own teams, and add your own help contacts at the end. For a few questions repeated every couple of weeks, the pulse survey format fits better. Emergent builds either one from a plain description instead of a template.

faq_plan.q: What are some mental health survey examples?
faq_plan.a: Three examples outside the office: a school sending teachers a check-in two weeks before exams, a sports club surveying players after the season, and a volunteer hotline checking on its call takers each month. Each stays under 10 questions and ends on a screen with help numbers. On Emergent, every answer goes to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Who runs the World Mental Health Surveys?
faq_plan.a: The World Health Organization's World Mental Health Survey Initiative runs them from its base at Harvard Medical School. Its structured, face-to-face surveys have reached more than 150,000 adults across 29 countries. The results describe whole populations. Treat them as national context for your own check-in, not as a benchmark for one team.

faq_plan.q: Do mental health survey reports say employers are doing enough?
faq_plan.ref: are employers doing enough for employee mental health surveys reports
faq_plan.a: Only partly, by workers' own account. In the American Psychological Association's 2023 Work in America survey, the majority were satisfied with their employer's mental health support. Yet more than half agreed their employer thinks the workplace is a lot mentally healthier than it actually is. Repeat your questions yearly, as with a brand awareness survey, to see a trend.

faq_plan.q: What do mental health surveys show about exercise?
faq_plan.ref: does exercise improve mental health survey
faq_plan.a: They link it to fewer bad days. A 2018 study in The Lancet Psychiatry found that people who exercised had 1.49 fewer days of poor mental health in the past month than people who did not. Treat that as a link rather than proof of cause. If your check-in asks about exercise, ask for days per week instead of a yes or no.

faq_plan.q: Do mental health surveys link social media use to poor mental health?
faq_plan.ref: does social media affect mental health survey
faq_plan.a: Yes, for teenagers. A 2019 study of US adolescents found that those who spend more than 3 hours per day using social media may be at heightened risk for mental health problems. If you survey students about it, ask for daily hours in bands and make 3 hours one of the cutoffs.

faq_plan.q: How do you analyze mental health surveys?
faq_plan.ref: how to analyze mental health surveys
faq_plan.a: Compare each group with its own previous round, not with the company average, and look only at groups above your minimum size. Then read the comments from the group with the biggest drop first. A church survey or a staff check-in can follow the same order. Emergent builds the results dashboard with the survey, with each team's score beside its last one.

plan.angle: The top 10 is screening tests (MHA, Psychology Today, a hospital, Penn State), statistics (NIMH, WHO) and clinical measures (APA, AHRQ); no page shows an organization how to run its own mental health check-in. This page is for the HR lead, nurse manager or program coordinator who needs one: no names stored, team scores shown only above a minimum, the same statements every round, a support screen with the EAP number and the 988 Lifeline after a low answer, and a call request kept apart from the ratings, all in a database the organization owns. It never presents the survey as a screen or a diagnosis, and the FAQ answers the research searches (World Mental Health Surveys, exercise, social media, employer reports) from primary sources.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Mental Health Survey With Anonymous Answers'; hero 127 chars with the primary and 'Build'; how-to description one sentence of 124 chars.

intent.evidence: Follows the brief's YMYL angle (an organization wellbeing check-in, not a clinical screen): no sentence presents the survey as a screen or diagnosis ('Leave diagnosis questions to clinicians.'), the low answer routes to the EAP and 988, and the FAQ answers the research searches from primary sources.

specificity.evidence: Team minimum of 8, Staff Support call list, QR code in the break room, week 1 vs week 8 for a funder, Not coping well on question 2.

openers.evidence: Full-sentence openers: 'Each answer is saved with the team and the date...', 'Write down the one decision the answers will feed...', 'The morning after a bus collision at its North depot...'.

craft.evidence: One ', so' ending (Q5 under limit); no run-on lists over 40 words.

voice.evidence: Calm and specific ('call the number yourself to check it'); the counting subheading and loose link analogies are notes.

truth.evidence: hero_description 'stores no names', feature_1 'No names, emails, or logins stored', prompt_chip_1 'No Names Stored' and howto_step_6_des 'confirm that no row holds a name' are contradicted by feature_5 'A yes saves a first name and phone number to a separate list' and tab_content_2 'Her first name and phone number went to the call list'. Third-party facts are inside their spans (APA 'the majority' and 'more than half' match 77% and 55%; WHO-5, Lancet Psychiatry 1.49 days, 3 hours a day, WMH 150,000 adults / 29 countries, 988).

distinct.evidence: Distinct from the wellness survey sibling: anonymity rules, support screen and call list; no sibling primary in a heading.

faq.evidence: 10 questions, each answered first; hub link in item 2; links to pulse survey, brand awareness survey, church survey; no brand or file format in a question; secondaries carried.
